name: Onondaga
confidence_why: 2 independent first-hand descriptions agree (1 state the same rule, 0 refine it); none contradicts.
catalog_quote: Main stress is normally penultimate, but can be final or antepenultimate under special circumstances. It can be analyzed with a syllabic trochee, with stressed suffixes and extrametrical suffixes.
sweep_summary: Both works with stress in the title are the same work: Michelson's 1983 Harvard PhD (Glottolog 160828 hh and 136545 mpieva; the mpieva 'Cambridge' school is an error), published in revised form as Michelson 1988, A Comparative Study of Lake-Iroquoian Accent (Kluwer), the dedicated first-hand accent study behind Hayes 1995:266. No open full-text copy exists (ProQuest/UMI; Springer paywalled with JS challenge; archive.org lending-only, djvu/search-inside refused; HathiTrust search-only;4 'Onondaga Accent' (pp. 90-91): utterance-final words have penultimate stress by default (joiner included); a few final morphemes attract final stress, a few repel stress to the antepenult; utterance-medially stress is generally word-final; and (p. 91) highest pitch can separate from strongest stress. The 1983 dissertation snippets say the same ('a rule of penultimate stress identical to the Mohawk Stress Rule and Oneida Stress Rule'; utterance-medial final stress). This confirms penultimate as the position but contradicts the catalog's classification fixed-strict: recommend reclassification to fixed-penultimate dominant (non-strict) with the morphological and utterance-medial exceptions, citing Michelson 1988:90-91 in place of the Abrams 2006 footnote / Hayes summary. Full pp. 90-97 (morpheme lists, fn. 40) and Woodbury 2018 ch. 2 remain high-priority acquisitions. Everything downloaded is with a line.

new_statements.quote: The majority of words in utterance-final position have penultimate stress. In Onondaga this is true also of words with a penultimate joiner; recall that the joiner could not be accented in PLI (cf. section 3.1.). Final stress occurs when the final morpheme in the word is one of a few morphemes that attract stress in this position; similarly, antepenultimate stress occurs when the final morpheme in the word is one of a few morphemes that repel stress. In utterance-medial position, stress is generally word-final, but a few suffixes that cannot be stressed condition penultimate stress.

new_statements.reading: Penultimate stress is the default for utterance-final (citation-form) words, joiner vowels counting as syllables; a small closed set of final morphemes attracts final stress and another small set repels stress onto the antepenult; utterance-medially stress is generally word-final. So Onondaga is fixed-penultimate as the dominant pattern with morphologically conditioned final/antepenultimate exceptions and a phrase-position alternation, not exceptionless penultimate: keep position=penultimate, drop counts as exceptionless (the strict set) (move to the dominant set), and note the utterance-medial final-stress rule and the pitch/stress separation (p. 91). Caveat: text recovered from overlapping verbatim snippets (Google Books feed + OpenLibrary search-inside of the archive.org scanned), not from an open full-text copy; the stitched passage is consistent across both sources and with the held Hayes 1995:266 summary and the on-disk Julian 2010 pins to Michelson 1988:90-97.

new_statements.quote: Onondaga has a rule of penultimate stress that is identical to the Mohawk Stress Rule and Oneida Stress Rule. Under certain conditions high pitch (and perhaps also strong stress) occurs on the antepenult or even on the preantepenult, but until more data are available it is not clear exactly what these conditions are. [4.1:] Therefore in modern Onondaga, high pitch and strong stress may occur on different syllables. [...] Onondaga has antepenultimate high pitch and penultimate stress whereas Mohawk has antepenultimate stress and high pitch. [3.7:] In utterance-medial position certain forms have final stress whereas the corresponding utterance-final forms have penultimate or prepenultimate stress.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is penultimate by a rule identical to the Mohawk and Oneida stress rules; in the dissertation's analysis the joiner/epenthetic-vowel question is handled by letting stress count the surface penult while high pitch may still fall on the antepenult (or preantepenult), so pitch and stress separate. In utterance-medial position some forms take final stress where the utterance-final form has penultimate (or prepenultimate) stress. Conditions for antepenultimate/preantepenultimate strong stress are left open ('until more data are available').

tone_statements.quote: As mentioned above, Onondaga has penultimate word accent with the exception of some words containing certain morphemes, some of which attract stress to the antepenultimate syllable and others to the final syllable. The penultimate accent is manifested in the phonology by tonic lengthening of vowels in an open syllable. Phonetically it is said to be realized with greater amplitude and with higher pitch in words of less than four syllables. While a separation of highest pitch and stress in words with penultimate stress is said to occur only in words of four or more syllables, words with final stress always exhibit a separation of stress and pitch.

tone.quote: By OO-21, high pitch has separated from accent and moved to the vowel of the preceding syllable; if the vowel of the preceding syllable was the joiner vowel * / a /, high pitch instead occurred on the vowel of the syllable preceding the joiner vowel ( e.g. PNI * / knoɁˈtsjaɁkeh / '(on) my tooth' ³⁸⁰ > Oo. / knóɁˈtsjaɁkeh /; PNI * / kaˈtsistajẽɁ / 'there is a fire' ³⁰⁶ ⁴⁵⁹ > Oo. / katsíˈstaːjẽɁ / 'there is a fireplace'; PNI * / waˈhetkẽɁ / 'it is bad' ¹³² > Oo. / wáˈhetkẽɁ /; cf. also Michelson 1988:92 and Woodbury 2003:60 ). This change may or may not have been present in Archaic and Old Onondaga; it must follow OO-11. (cf. also Mithun 1979:174).
